meta.title: smartSQL — Software for people who work in data
meta.description: smartSQL designs and sells software for teams who write, model, and ship SQL. Meet the current product, the catalog that came before it, and the people building what is next.

hero.body: We build and sell tools that keep queries, models, and pipelines close enough to touch. smartSQL is the workspace we ship today.

platform.title: The database, close enough to touch.
platform.body: smartSQL is for teams who are done treating the database as a ticket queue. The workspace we sell puts the question, the schema, and the result in one place, so the work stays legible as it grows.

items.name: smartSQL
items.description: The product for sale now. A workspace for writing and reviewing SQL with the schema held in view.

docs.heading: Overview
paragraphs: smartSQL is the workspace we sell for writing, reviewing, and sharing SQL without losing the schema that gives a query its meaning.
Add, remove, or reorder sections in this list to grow the documentation. Each section needs an id, a heading, and one or more paragraphs.

docs.heading: The workspace
paragraphs: The editor keeps the question, the tables it touches, and the result in one view. A reviewer can see the shape of a query before reading every line.
Saved work stays attached to the model it was written against, so a later change in the schema is visible next to the statement that depends on it.

docs.heading: Review
paragraphs: A query is ready to share when the intent, the joins, and the expected result are all still readable. smartSQL keeps those three in the same place.
Use this section for the review checklist your team actually follows. Add a paragraph for each rule you want readers to see.

docs.heading: Extending this page
paragraphs: This page is the home for the long-form notes about smartSQL. Drop in guides, examples, and operating details as separate sections.
Nothing on this page is fixed in the layout. The catalog card opens whatever sections you list for this product.

items.name: Ledgerline
items.description: A past product for watching data jobs the way an operator watches a live signal.

docs.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Ledgerline was our product for watching data jobs as a live signal: what started, what stalled, and what changed the result downstream.
The notes below are a starting shelf. Replace them with the runbooks and references you want to keep for this product.

docs.heading: Reading the signal
paragraphs: Each job leaves a trace you can follow from the first read to the last write. The point is to see the break without reconstructing the pipeline from logs.
Add the signals your operators actually watch, one section at a time.

docs.heading: When a job fails
paragraphs: A failed run should say which step stopped, which inputs it had already accepted, and which outputs never landed.
Use the paragraphs here for the incident notes you want on call to find first.

items.name: Northframe
items.description: A past product for drawing a model before the tables settled into place.

docs.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Northframe was our product for drawing a model before the tables locked in. It kept names, relationships, and open questions in one picture.
Treat this page as the binder for that work. Add a section whenever there is more to explain.

docs.heading: Shaping a model
paragraphs: Start from the questions the data has to answer, then name the entities that carry those answers. Northframe held that conversation before the migration.

docs.heading: Handing a model to SQL
paragraphs: A model is ready to become tables when every relationship has a direction, a name, and a reason. The handoff notes live in this section.
